title: Stages of Change Visualizer
description: Step five people through the Transtheoretical Model's five Stages of Change (Precontemplation, Contemplation, Preparation, Action, Maintenance). An info panel gives the definition, motivational state, stage-matched intervention, and a smoking-cessation example for the selected person's stage. Relapse arrows from Action and Maintenance show relapse as an expected part of change.
creator: Introduction to Public Health Project
subject: public health
health behavior
Transtheoretical Model
Stages of Change
smoking cessation
relapse
learning_objective: Explain how the recommended intervention changes across the five Stages of Change and why relapse is treated as an expected part of the change process.

educational.topic: Transtheoretical Model and Stages of Change
learningObjectives: Name the five Stages of Change in order
Explain how the stage-matched intervention differs at each stage
Explain why relapse is expected and is not a sign of failure
prerequisites: Basic idea of health behavior change

controls.label: ← Back / ← Relapse
controls.description: Moves the selected person back one stage. From Action or Maintenance it is a relapse and returns the person to Contemplation.

controls.label: Forward →
controls.description: Moves the selected person to the next stage.

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns all five people to Precontemplation.

controls.label: Person icons
controls.description: Click a person icon to select it.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Step-through with concrete stage content visible at every step
keyQuestions: What should a practitioner do differently for a person in Precontemplation than for a person in Preparation?
Why does the model draw relapse as a normal path?
commonMisconceptions: Relapse means the person or the intervention failed
One action-oriented program fits people at every stage
People move through the stages once, in a straight line
assessmentOpportunities: Match a described person to a stage and an intervention
Explain why an action-oriented class is a poor match for a precontemplator
